v1.feedback: The tree-to-Möbius morph is the right structural idea — real half-twist math (theta*0.5) and the palette pivot from bark/chlorophyll greens to silver-chrome sells the swerve. Two things to tighten: the intermediate morph states (uTwist ~0.4–0.6) compress the tree into an amorphous ring that doesn't read as either form — consider easing uTwist with a sharper sigmoid or adding a brief hold at 0/1 so each shape registers for at least 3 seconds before transitioning. Second, in full Möbius mode the particle density thins on the outer radius because the L-system trunk segments (gen 0–1) cluster near s≈0; redistribute particles more uniformly along the strip width or scale s non-linearly so the strip surface reads as a continuous band rather than a sparse halo with a dense spine.

v2.feedback: The tree→Möbius morph is a legitimate 'swerve' and both endpoint forms are readable mathematical shapes the brief rewards; the tonal shift from warm bark-green to cold chrome is restrained and intentional. However, the linear mix between two topologically different forms likely creates a ~2s illegible intermediate cloud — consider easing particles along geodesic arcs or staggering the morph by generation so branches peel off sequentially into the strip. The Möbius R=4.5 may also feel small relative to the tree's vertical extent; scale it up or tighten the camera during twist phase so the strip fills frame properly.
